monument_name: Tarpibaḍā Śikhara Temple 1 (built around the 13th-15th centuries)
description_en: Tarpibaḍā Śikhara Temple 1, built around the 13th-15th centuries, is the larger of two śikhara temples that face each other and are located about 20 meters north of a stone fountain (JUM0443). The three monuments (twośikharatemples and the stone fountain) are situated on the eastern bank of the Sinja River, opposite the villages of Jacha (to the south-west) and Tarpibaḍā (to the north-west). The Temples and the fountain are built on terraces that are currently planted with apple trees. The monuments are described by D. R. Sharma (Sharma 2012: 192-193).The Temple 1 faces east, and its pediment is embellished with carved horizontal friezes. The doorjambs are also decorated with losanges and spirals. In the centre of the door lintel is carved the image of a four-armed character, possibly Gaṇeśa. The ceiling, too, is carved with a lotus in the centre and geometrical motifs on the spandrels. The sanctum is empty. It might have contained aśivaliṅga.Elements from anotherśikharatemple are scattered around the site. They could have originated from a third temple that stood next to the two existing monuments, or from a separate group.From the 13th to the 15th centuries, suchśikharatemples were built throughout the Karnali Basin (Andolfatto 2019). The rarity of inscriptions onśikharatemples (locally known asdevala) complicates dating of these monuments. Two similar temples can be found a few kilometres to the north of the site, above the village of Sanjyalbada (JUM0510), and date from the 13th-15th centuries. The similarity of the two sites' plans suggests that the Tarpibaḍā Temple1 and 2 were also constructed around the same time. This dates to the end of the Khaśa Malla kingdom (12th-14th century) and the reign of the Kalyāl dynasty from Jumla (15th century).
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université. Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
